summary: Registers the Namespace Identifier ieee for URNs that name resources published by IEEE, with management handled by the IEEE Registration Authority.

plainLanguage.summary: Gives IEEE its own name prefix for labeling its things so they do not clash.

questions: what is the ieee urn namespace
how do you create an ieee urn
subtitle: Namespace identifier ieee for URNs identifying IEEE resources

tldr.problem: IEEE publishes many standardized resources such as networking standards and YANG data models, and needs a unique, persistent namespace for assigning and managing identifiers to these resources.
tldr.mechanism: This document registers the namespace identifier 'ieee' for Uniform Resource Names, structured as urn:ieee:{IEEEresource}:{ResourceSpecificString}, with the IEEE Registration Authority managing the assignment and uniqueness of identifiers within this namespace.
tldr.outcome: IEEE and other organizations can now use the registered ieee namespace to create persistent, globally unique identifiers for IEEE resources that will not conflict with other URN namespaces.

today: RFC 8069 remains the defining document for the ieee URN namespace. It is registered with IANA as a formal URN namespace and continues to be used by IEEE to identify and manage its standards, data models, and other published resources.

sections.title: IEEE and the Need for a URN Namespace
sections.content:
The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) is a major standards-setting organization whose work includes electrical engineering, electronics, telecommunications, and computer engineering. Within IEEE, standardization activities are organized into sponsors and working groups such as the LAN/MAN Standards Committee and groups like 802.1 and 802.3.

As IEEE creates technical specifications, it needs to maintain identifiers in a managed namespace that is unique and persistent. A Uniform Resource Name, or URN, is a special kind of identifier that is designed to be globally unique and never change, even if the resource moves or is accessed differently. To use URNs for IEEE resources, IEEE needed to register a special namespace identifier to ensure that its URN identifiers would not conflict with those of other organizations.
sections.plainLanguage: IEEE creates lots of technical standards. It needed its own name prefix so that when it names something with a permanent label, nobody else can use that same label for something different.

sections.title: URN Structure and Namespace Identifier
sections.content:
A Uniform Resource Name (URN) is a type of identifier designed for persistent naming. The syntax for a URN is urn:Namespace-ID:Namespace-Specific-String. The Namespace Identifier (NID) is a short code like 'isbn' for books or 'urn' for generic names, and the Namespace Specific String identifies the particular resource within that namespace.

For IEEE, the registered Namespace Identifier is ieee. The full structure is urn:ieee:{IEEEresource}:{ResourceSpecificString}, where 'IEEEresource' defines a class of IEEE resource (for example, 'std' for standards or 'yang' for YANG data models) and 'ResourceSpecificString' identifies a particular resource within that class. Both parts are case-insensitive, allowing flexibility in usage.
sections.plainLanguage: A URN is like a permanent address label. IEEE's label starts with urn:ieee: and then describes what the thing is and its specific name.

sections.title: Registration Authority and Management
sections.content:
The IEEE Registration Authority (IEEE RA) is the organizational unit responsible for managing the IEEE URN namespace. The IEEE RA maintains a registration authority that manages the assignment of new 'IEEEresource' types and the specific registration values assigned for each resource class. The procedures are documented and published by IEEE RA on its website at standards.ieee.org.

The IEEE RA is responsible for ensuring the uniqueness of the strings themselves and may permit secondary responsibility for management of well-defined sub-trees. IEEE will update documentation of registered uses as needed, and the registration tables are published and maintained by the IEEE RA on its web site. The namespace is global in scope, meaning URNs registered in the ieee namespace are valid everywhere.
sections.plainLanguage: IEEE has a team that keeps the registry of all the names it has given out, making sure no two things get the same name.

sections.title: Example URNs
sections.content:
The RFC provides examples of URNs that could be assigned by the IEEE RA. One example is urn:ieee:std:802.5:yang, which identifies the YANG data model for the IEEE 802.5 standard (token ring). Another example is urn:ieee:foobar, which illustrates that new resource types can be created as needed.

While YANG data modeling (a protocol configuration language) was a catalyst for creating this namespace, the ieee namespace is designed to be flexible enough to support whatever resource types IEEE may need to identify in the future. The examples show how the structure allows for hierarchical organization of identifiers.
sections.plainLanguage: One name might be for a standard like 802.5 and its YANG model. Another name is just a made-up example to show how the system works.
